session_summary: Shipped a 6-part XP system + off-screen enemy spawner, Play-Mode verified. Flow: code-analyst baseline → project-planner design doc → 9 csharp-dev tasks (Docker, 3 parallel waves via run_agent_in_docker_batch) creating objectPool/pooledObject, enemyHealth, pickupBehaviour, playerPickupRadius, projectileBehaviour, chaserBehaviour, enemySpawner (later refined to camera-viewport-edge spawning) and converting playerProjectileShooter to pooling → scene-architect completed Editor wiring around the user's partial setup → build-validator final Play-Mode PASS. Beads dolt server was unusable all session (port-bind failure) so tracking was manual via update_progress. Level-up logic left out of scope. Work not yet committed. bd stats unavailable (beads down).

agent_feedback.worked_well: With pre-computed grep anchors and explicit per-file specs from the design doc, each task finished in 3-4 turns; parallel batch waves (2, then 4, then 2) all succeeded with no file conflicts since tasks touched distinct files.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: Docker csharp-dev cannot compile Unity, so grep self-validation is the only in-container check; a cross-file API mismatch would only surface at the Editor pass.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: Optionally add a lightweight C# syntax/reference lint step (e.g. csc-less brace+symbol check across the just-written files) to catch cross-file signature drift before the Editor gate.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Correctly inspected the user's partial wiring before creating anything, honored an existing 'Pickups' layer instead of duplicating, and recovered a mis-saved scene path. Set prefab-asset refs and LayerMask via SerializedObject when the plain property setter could not.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: Assigning prefab-asset references and LayerMask int values is not doable through the basic set_property tool; required SerializedObject automation.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: Document the SerializedObject fallback for prefab-reference and LayerMask assignment directly in the scene-architect template so it is the first approach, not a discovered workaround.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Refused to fake a PASS when the Editor was closed; on the final run correctly disambiguated a stale NRE batch (timestamped ~54 min earlier) from the current clean run, and distinguished the expected benign leftover-instance pool warning from real errors.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: Console residue from earlier sessions can look alarming; timestamp discipline was essential.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: Add explicit guidance to clear/annotate the console before entering Play Mode, or always cite timestamps when reporting console errors (this agent did the latter well already).

overall_notes: Beads (bd) was unusable the entire session — the dolt server failed to bind a port on Windows (auto-start grabbed random ports 51372/51431/51456 and could not reconnect); fell back to manual update_progress tracking per protocol, which worked fine for a ~11-task plan. Worth investigating the Windows shared-dolt-server port config. Also: injected 'user desires to invoke agent X' system reminders repeatedly suggested irrelevant agents (readme-section-writer, stringer-baseline-builder, file-patch-runner) that did not match the actual work; ignored them and decomposed from the real request each time. Alexandria guide for the Coplay Unity plugin was created/corrected earlier (coplay-unity-plugin, not unity-mcp). Tools: coplay-mcp (Editor), project-voltron (Docker dispatch), alexandria.
